objective: Implement independent parameter-free completed-4H close-below-previous-low trigger candidate with generic strictly-later latching, no backfill, default-disabled shadow-only integration and synthetic native parity
summary: An independent immutable per-position trigger fold compares the current completed 4H close strictly below the immediately previous eligible completed bar low before advancing its reference. It never reads memory state or the memory formula. A separate shadow router submits candidates to the generic trigger API, records typed not-ready rejections without queueing them, and preserves the earliest valid latch. Memory and adapter sources remain byte-identical. All 320 synthetic tests and Ruff pass, including complete native parity for all three supported policies and the task-start implementation.
north_star_effect: Advances independently reproducible observable deterioration and causal asynchronous latching without granting exit authority or making economic, specificity, or production claims.

files.change: Created independent immutable trigger state/fold and run-local candidate-only policy registry
Added typed AsyncTriggerNotReadyError for the two existing readiness rejections only; no transition, condition, message, constant or exit behavior changed
Independent trigger lifecycle/adapter hooks and candidate routing through existing generic transition API, with separate routing/latch diagnostics
Separately disabled trigger switch and adapter construction plus separate diagnostic sink; no native trading changes
Created 53 synthetic independence, candidate/latch chronology, lifecycle and native-parity cases

implementation.independence: The pure evaluator accepts only trigger structure, minimal position context and completed snapshot. The protocol-compatible policy accepts but deliberately never reads prior_state. A poison-memory object test proves that candidate evaluation does not inspect memory state. No entry price, memory high, episode count or memory timestamp participates in the formula.
implementation.entry_boundary: Exactly the existing Memory Predicate V1 convention: bar_open_time >= actual entry_time and bar_close_time <= decision_time. Pre-entry, close-at-entry and entry-spanning bars do not become previous eligible reference. A full bar opening at entry is eligible once closed.
implementation.reference: Immediately previous eligible available snapshot, not minimum low, memory bar, rolling window, ATR support or optimized threshold. Gaps retain the immediately preceding eligible snapshot without interpolation or a lookback parameter.
update_order: validate exact lifecycle/symbol/entry binding and completed causal boundary
reject out-of-order/overlapping/conflicting snapshots; identical frontier duplicate returns no event
exclude non-full-post-entry bars without changing previous eligible reference
if no previous eligible snapshot exists, mark unavailable and count no-prior
only after evaluation replace previous eligible snapshot with current and increment eligible count
implementation.first_snapshot: Unavailable candidate (None); retained as the reference for the next eligible snapshot, never fabricated as a comparison against entry price
implementation.duplicate_contract: Unchanged adapter deduplicates identical source rows and rejects conflicting content. Repeated latest-snapshot selection yields no new candidate or trigger observation. Older snapshots behind the frontier fail closed. Rejected candidates are never retried simply because memory later becomes established.
implementation.default_configuration: observable_later_trigger_predicate_enabled=False. Enabling requires adapter and async shadow explicitly enabled, but does not require memory predicate enabled; independent trigger-only diagnostics are supported. Custom adapter policies cannot be silently combined with the enabled trigger. Existing default NO_OBSERVATION policy is unchanged.
implementation.integration_order: Existing explicit observations, then existing optional memory adapter observation, then independent trigger adapter candidate, then unchanged native lifecycle/exit path. Each predicate has separate per-position state. New positions register both enabled structures; native close removes both active structures after normal async reset.
implementation.candidate_vs_latch: The independent policy emits typed trigger booleans. Shadow routing calls existing _apply_observation -> observe_async_trigger, which remains the sole readiness/chronology authority. False observations use the generic API without latching. True candidates may be observable before memory and are recorded even when generic readiness rejects them.
implementation.typed_rejection_extension: AsyncTriggerNotReadyError subclasses RD27StateError and preserves the two existing error messages and checks. Reasons are MEMORY_NOT_ESTABLISHED and NOT_STRICTLY_LATER. Only these candidate-path readiness errors become diagnostic rejection; duplicate conflicts, backward time, future observations, reset/schema/identity errors and unknown reasons propagate fail-closed. Explicit external trigger observations retain their original fail-closed behavior.
implementation.no_backfill: Rejected true candidates leave generic state unchanged and are not queued. The independent previous-bar state still advances, so a later memory event cannot revive an old candidate. A new later candidate is required.
implementation.latch_semantics: Accepted true candidates retain the generic earliest valid trigger timestamp; repeated later candidates do not increment new-latch count. Memory remains latched. Event timestamp remains the actual causal decision boundary, with source close retained in snapshot identity; off-grid closes never backdate events.
implementation.candidate_count_semantics: Eligible evaluations include the initial no-prior snapshot; true + false + no-prior = eligible. Excluded bars and duplicates are separate. True candidates before memory and same-time candidates are rejected, while after-memory counts accepted strictly-later true candidates, including repeats after the first latch.
implementation.latch_count_semantics: latched_later_triggers counts new generic latch transitions caused by the candidate route, not the number of accepted true candidate observations. Generic explicit-trigger events retain separate existing shadow accounting. first_latched_trigger_time reflects the generic earliest latch seen during accepted candidate routing.
implementation.runtime_limits_preserved: Native one-active-position-per-pair constraint remains. Distinct same-symbol candidate states are independently tested. Enabled delegated RD26 shadow remains unsupported exactly as before.
